nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Turn any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into a persistent queryable knowledge graph with an honest EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail; community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

nodes.label: Fast Path: Query Existing Graph
nodes.source_location: ## What You Must Do When Invoked
nodes.rationale: When graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, skip the entire build pipeline and run graphify query immediately - the graph is already built, rebuilding wastes tokens and time.

nodes.label: AST Structural Extraction (Part A)
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted deterministically via AST with no LLM and no API key - a code-only corpus skips semantic extraction entirely, so graphify never blocks on a key.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction via Parallel Subagents (Part B)
nodes.rationale: Docs/papers/images are extracted by LLM subagents dispatched in parallel in a single message (5-10x faster than reading files one-by-one); must use general-purpose agents because read-only Explore agents cannot write chunk files, silently dropping results.
nodes.norm_label: semantic extraction via parallel subagents (part b)

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache is checked before dispatching any subagents so only uncached files cost tokens; stale .graphify_cached.json from prior runs is deleted so Part C never merges stale results.

nodes.label: Graph Health Check Gate
nodes.rationale: Read-only diagnostic before labeling that surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints, and self-loops - the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. Never aborts, but warnings must be surfaced per the Honesty Rules.

nodes.label: Graph Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write a graph smaller than the existing graph.json, so an empty or failed extraction can never clobber a good graph, report, or analysis sidecar.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS when unsure), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, show raw cohesion numbers, warn before visualizing >5000 nodes - the audit trail is the product.

nodes.label: Discrete Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges - the bimodal distribution observed in production (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) showed range guidance being collapsed to a binary, so INFERRED edges must pick from a fixed set of five values and never default to 0.5.

nodes.label: Full-Path Node ID Format
nodes.rationale: IDs use the full repo-relative path (every directory level) so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and semantic IDs match AST-generated IDs; filename-only or immediate-parent IDs create orphan ghost-duplicate nodes, and chunk-number suffixes break determinism.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: The query matcher is case-folded substring + IDF only - no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching - so the question is expanded against the graph's actual label vocabulary (max 12 tokens, never invented) to prevent 0-hit collapse while keeping the expansion auditable.

nodes.label: BFS/DFS Graph Traversal
nodes.rationale: BFS (depth 3) for broad 'what is X connected to' context; DFS (depth 6) for tracing a specific dependency chain; output is token-budget ranked and truncated. Answer only from what the graph contains - never hallucinate edges.

nodes.label: Save-Result Work-Memory Loop
nodes.rationale: Every answered query is saved back into the graph with an outcome tag (useful/dead_end/corrected) so the next --update extracts the Q&A as a node; graphify reflect compiles LESSONS.md listing preferred sources, known dead ends, and corrections - a self-improving loop across sessions.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts new/changed files against the saved manifest; code-only changes skip semantic extraction entirely (no LLM), and changed video files must be transcribed first or raw media paths reach subagents unreadable.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-extract
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction is preserved (#801); prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files because changed files are handled by replace-on-re-extract - pruning changed files would delete the freshly re-extracted content (#1178/#1344); root= relativization keeps prune paths matching graph paths (#1361).

nodes.label: Cluster-Only Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Self-contained CLI command that re-clusters, relabels, and regenerates outputs from the existing graph; Steps 5-9 must NOT be re-run because they read intermediate files a prior build's cleanup already deleted (#1392).

nodes.label: Whisper Transcription with Domain Hint
nodes.rationale: The host agent composes a one-sentence domain hint from god-node labels and passes it as Whisper's initial prompt (no separate API call); JSON must be written from Python, not shell redirect, because Whisper prints progress to stdout (#1392).

nodes.label: URL Ingestion (/graphify add)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects URL type (YouTube via yt-dlp, Twitter via oEmbed, arXiv, PDF, images, webpages via html2text), saves to ./raw, then runs the --update pipeline to merge the new file into the existing graph.

nodes.label: Watch Mode Auto-Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Background watcher with 3s debounce so a wave of parallel agent writes triggers one rebuild, not one per file; code changes rebuild via AST with no LLM, doc changes only flag needs_update for a manual --update.

nodes.label: Graph Export Targets (Wiki/Neo4j/FalkorDB/SVG/GraphML)
nodes.rationale: Each export runs only on its own flag; Cypher exports use MERGE so re-runs are idempotent; FalkorDB prefers direct push because GRAPH.QUERY has no bulk script import.

nodes.label: Graphify MCP stdio Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live; Claude Desktop config must use the absolute interpreter path because it cannot run shell substitution.

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Only runs when total_words > 5000 - for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: Cross-Repo / Monorepo Graph Merge
nodes.rationale: Repos are cloned into ~/.graphify/repos and each subfolder is extracted via the CLI directly (which places graphify-out inside the scanned path) because the skill pipeline would clobber a shared graphify-out; merged nodes carry a repo attribute for origin filtering.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit with no background process; detects changed code files via git diff HEAD~1 and re-runs AST extraction only - doc/image changes still require a manual --update; appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration (graphify claude install)
nodes.rationale: Writes a '## graphify' section to the project CLAUDE.md so every future Claude Code session checks the graph before answering codebase questions and rebuilds after code changes - always-on without manual /graphify.

nodes.label: Spring Boot REST API (bodhassess-api-spring)
nodes.rationale: Spring Boot 2.5.5 on Java 11 with standard controller/service/repository layering, no JPA associations (plain String UUID columns, mostly client-supplied IDs), JSON columns via hibernate-types-52, and the deprecated WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter style kept deliberately - match it, don't modernize piecemeal.

nodes.label: React SPA (bodhassess-app)
nodes.rationale: React 19 + Vite 7 SPA where the @ alias resolves to the app root (not src/); roughly 37 of ~60 routes are static template mockups that never touch the API - the wired surface is dashboard, assessments, question-bank create/item-explorer, qualities, reports, admin, and portal.

nodes.label: run.sh Top-Level Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Only the top-level run.sh should be used - the nested bodhassess-api-spring/run.sh starts MySQL without Redis so heartbeat features fail; run.sh never sources the root .env, so host-run API and Vite only see exported variables.

nodes.label: Hand-Managed MySQL Schema (01-schema.sql)
nodes.rationale: ddl-auto=none so Hibernate never creates or migrates anything; the schema file runs only on first container init, and the established migration pattern is idempotent INFORMATION_SCHEMA count checks + PREPARE/EXECUTE ALTER blocks inside the same file - adding a column means editing CREATE TABLE and adding such a block.

nodes.label: PortalSession as Assessment Instance
nodes.rationale: 'Assessment' has no entity - AssessmentsController/Service/Dto all operate on PortalSession (portal_sessions), a respondent's assigned assessment instance with answers, mqt_scores, and demographics as JSON columns; distinct from the inert IRT-side Session entity.

nodes.label: Client-Side MQT Scoring
nodes.rationale: The backend never computes scores - mqt_scores and the score summary string are computed in the browser on the portal take page and PUT to the API, which persists them without validation.

nodes.label: Questionnaire Name as Business Key
nodes.rationale: Create dual-writes instruments and published_questionnaires rows with the same name, create dedupes by name (deleteOthersByName), catalog delete cascades across three tables by name, and the portal take page looks the questionnaire up by name - so renaming a published questionnaire breaks every pending assessment referencing the old name.

nodes.label: Dual Questionnaire Models (published_questionnaires vs instruments)
nodes.rationale: QuestionnairesService targets PublishedQuestionnaire while QuestionnairesCatalogService targets the instruments table via native SQL through EntityManager - the QuestionnaireCatalog entity and repository are dead code; 'instrument' and 'questionnaire/catalog' are used interchangeably.

nodes.label: Inert IRT/Adaptive Scaffolding
nodes.rationale: Session carries theta_estimate/trust_score, items has irt_a/b/c, instruments has is_adaptive/scoring_config - but no code computes theta or selects items adaptively; SessionsService is read-only native SQL, and tenants/users tables have no entity at all.

nodes.label: DOB-as-Credential JWT Auth
nodes.rationale: Stateless JWT with three user types (ADMIN/PRACTITIONER/RESPONDENT) and nobody has a password hash: admin is a single env-driven account with no DB row, practitioners and respondents log in with email-or-phone + date of birth; the token filter also accepts ?token= query params, and uploads plus questionnaire endpoints are deliberately public.

nodes.label: Heartbeat Polling Live Tracking
nodes.rationale: Pure polling, no WebSocket/SSE anywhere: the portal POSTs a heartbeat every 5s, HeartbeatService writes Redis keys heartbeat:<sessionId> with short TTLs (Redis's only use in the system), and the admin live-tracking page polls read-only endpoints.

nodes.label: Metronic 9 (KeenThemes) Template Base
nodes.rationale: Much of the template is unused (39 layout variants, only layout-1 used); leftover 'use client' directives and SSR guards are inert - don't propagate or strip them.

nodes.label: lib/api.ts Single API Client
nodes.rationale: Per-resource objects over a shared jsonFetch that throws on non-2xx; lib/data-store.ts re-exports these but swallows errors (lists return [], mutations return null), and its getSessions/getQuestionnaires/sessionsToReports are deliberate empty stubs - report pages render empty by design.

nodes.label: Portal Take Flow (src/pages/portal/take.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Where assessments actually happen: session id from ?id= query param, questionnaire fetched by name, disclaimer + demographics gates, heartbeats every 5s, first answer stamps started_at, submit computes all MQT scores in the browser and PUTs Completed - and if that final write fails the error is swallowed and the user still lands on /portal/complete.

nodes.label: Data-Driven Route Access (url_paths globs)
nodes.rationale: Roles carry url_paths glob patterns; canAccess() gates both PrivateRoute and the sidebar; admin is synthesized as a practitioner with url_paths ['/*'].

nodes.label: Three sessionStorage Auth Tokens
nodes.rationale: Practitioner, admin, and respondent tokens live under separate sessionStorage keys (never localStorage); the client attaches whichever exists in practitioner > admin > respondent priority, and practitioner/admin logins clear each other's token; portal pages bypass the auth provider and read sessionStorage directly.

nodes.label: Reverted 'sameer' Branch History
nodes.rationale: Branch sameer was merged then fully reverted, so commit messages advertise subsystems that do NOT exist in the working tree (Assessment entity, data-studio, unified auth, questionnaire versioning); trust the working tree, not git log - merging origin/sameer resurrects all of it as conflicts.

nodes.label: API Service (prod profile, Top-Level Compose)
nodes.rationale: Gated behind the prod compose profile so dev mode doesn't build the backend image; publishes on 127.0.0.1:4000 only - public TLS is delegated to the separate nginx stack.

nodes.label: Commented-Out Web Service
nodes.rationale: The web (built Vite SPA behind nginx) service exists only as a commented block - prod mode is half-retired and ships no web container.

nodes.label: Nested App Service (API Compose, prod profile)
nodes.norm_label: nested app service (api compose, prod profile)

nodes.label: Nginx TLS Proxy Service
nodes.rationale: Standalone compose stack for public TLS (api.bodh.biz) on ports 80/443 with letsencrypt certs mounted read-only; joins the API's Docker network via the external network name bodhassess-api_bodh rather than defining its own.

nodes.label: Stock Metronic Template README
nodes.rationale: This is the unmodified Metronic 9 template readme and is wrong for this project - it mentions Next.js 15 and Prisma/PostgreSQL, but the actual app is a Vite SPA with no Prisma; project CLAUDE.md says to ignore it.
